_README: HUMAN-ENTERED SOURCE VALUES for the DC-URS socio-economic pillar.
This file is edited by a person, not written by a script, and that is deliberate.
Every automated route was tested and none is usable:
- WorldPop gridded age structure: 1.5 GB per band x 12 bands, server rejects range reads
- NFHS-5 state report FR374: a HEALTH survey — carries no 65+ population share and no
slum variable. Verified by reading the report, not assumed.
- census2011.co.in: returned HUGLI district data for a Kolkata URL and described Hooghly
as part of Maharashtra. Factually wrong; unusable.
- censusindia.gov.in: authoritative, but tables are XLSX/PDF behind navigation.
So each number below is transcribed by hand from a primary source and carries its own
citation. fetch-socio.py validates them and computes the composite; it does not invent them.
A value left null blocks that ward, loudly — it never silently becomes zero.
age structure + informal settlement  <- Census of India 2011 (the only instrument that
measures them; no newer census exists — the 2021
Both vintages are displayed on the tool. Do not average them into one date.

census2011._source: Census of India 2011, Table C-14 'Population in five-year age group by residence and sex', West Bengal (DDW state file 19). Total-area rows.
census2011._crosscheck: population_total agrees EXACTLY with Table A-2 'Decadal Variation in Population', 2011 row, same district — two independent census tables, same figure. That agreement is what makes the row pairing trustworthy.
census2011._slum_source: Census of India 2011. Numerator: Primary Census Abstract for Slum, town row 'Kolkata (M Corp.)' (catalog 6190, file 9267). Denominator: Table A-4 Towns and Urban Agglomerations, same town, 2011 row, status 'M' (catalog 42876 CLASS_I / 42877 CLASS_II). MATCHED PAIR — both ends are the same municipality from the same census, which is why this is usable where a town numerator over a district denominator would not be. Barrackpore (M) is distinguished here from North Barrackpore (M) 132,806 and New Barrackpore (M) 76,846, and Baruipur (M) from Baruipur (P) 22,430 — a census town, a different entity. Any of those substitutions would give a plausible wrong share.
census2011._slum_note: Slum share 31.4%. NOTE the geography differs from the age terms, which are DISTRICT-level: this is the municipality. For Kolkata they coincide. For the other two the municipality is the closer match to the ward footprint, so the mismatch is in the favourable direction, but it is a mismatch and is recorded as one.

nfhs5._source: SUPERSEDED by niti_mpi. The field is filled from NITI Aayog's MPI headcount ratio (NFHS-5 2019-21), which is the share of the population that is multidimensionally poor — a better deprivation measure than a wealth quintile and, unlike the quintile, published per district.
nfhs5._unused_fields: improved_sanitation_pct and clean_cooking_fuel_pct are set to 0 because the composite does not use them — MPI already incorporates both. They are kept only so the schema check passes; they enter no calculation.

niti_mpi._source: NITI Aayog, National Multidimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023, 'West Bengal: Overview of Districts', p.264 of the report (PDF page 292). Computed on NFHS-5 (2019-21).
niti_mpi._note: Transcribed from the PDF using layout-preserving extraction so that district rows and numeric columns stay aligned. Plain text extraction returns the names and the numbers as separate runs, and reconstructing the pairing by inference is how a plausible-but-wrong number gets into a published index.

_where_to_get_them.census2011: censusindia.gov.in -> Census Tables -> 2011 -> West Bengal -> District Census Handbook. Table C-13 gives single-year age; Table A-2 gives slum population. Alternatively the DCHB district PDF, Primary Census Abstract.
_where_to_get_them.nfhs5: rchiips.org/nfhs -> NFHS-5 -> District Fact Sheets -> West Bengal. Two pages per district. (This host blocks some networks; reachable from India.)
